description:
Multiple unit tests advertise themselves as testing the InvalidArgument guard but never call the function under test. They re-implement the check locally and then assert the local check works.

Examples:
- src/methods/calendar.rs:127-141 (calendar_get_empty_id_returns_invalid_argument)
- src/methods/event.rs:194-208 (calendar_event_get_empty_id_returns_invalid_argument)
- src/methods/event_notification.rs:244-258 (calendar_event_notification_get_empty_id_guard)

The test body is:
```
let ids: &[&str] = &[""];
let mut found_error = false;
for id in ids.iter() { if id.is_empty() { found_error = true; break; } }
assert!(found_error, "empty id must trigger the InvalidArgument guard");
```

This proves only that `"".is_empty()` returns true. It does NOT call `calendar_get`, `calendar_event_get`, etc. The production guard could be deleted entirely and these tests would still pass — they have no oracle.

This violates AGENTS.md test-integrity rule: 'Never write a test that uses the code under test as its own oracle.' Worse, this test does not even reach the code under test.

Fix: convert to wiremock-backed tokio::test that calls the public method on a SessionClient and asserts the returned Result is `Err(ClientError::InvalidArgument(_))`. The infrastructure already exists in tests/helpers.rs:51 (make_client). Or delete these tests outright if a wiremock harness is unwanted — they currently provide negative value (false confidence).

Note: src/methods/event_parse.rs and src/methods/principal_availability.rs explicitly comment that the guards 'require a wiremock-backed async harness' — the harness exists. There is no reason these tests cannot exist.
title: Test claims to test guard but only re-asserts is_empty()
